Stage 4 of 5 · Rebuild

Rebuild

The crisis is over. Nobody is congratulating you any more. Life is quieter, and some days it's flat. This is where most of the actual healing happens, and nobody warns you how ordinary it feels.

You're here if

  • You've got a few months and the novelty has worn off
  • You're sleeping badly, eating rubbish, or both
  • Feelings you haven't had since you were a teenager are turning up unannounced
  • You're wondering what sober people actually do on a Saturday night

The job of this stage

Rebuild the machine, then start filling the hours with things that are yours. The first page explains what your brain is doing on its own schedule, which makes the flat days much easier to sit through. Then the body, then feelings, then the social life.

Read these, in this order

  1. How the brain healsWhy you feel flat, what's healing underneath, and roughly when.→
  2. The body comes firstFour daily practices, and the order to fix them in.→
  3. SleepWhy it gets worse before it gets better, and six things to lock in.→
  4. FoodStable food, stable mood. Foundations and a day you can repeat.→
  5. MovementThe fastest mood lever you have. The bar is low on purpose.→
  6. Feelings and meditationThe feelings come back loud. How to be with them without acting.→
  7. HobbiesFill the hours and build an identity that is not about drinking.→
  8. Social life without drinkingWhat to say, how to do a party, dating, and which friends stay.→
  9. If you slipA slip is common and it isn't the end. What to do in the next 24 hours.→

One habit for this stage

A thirty-second daily check-in. Hungry, angry, lonely, tired: most slips in this stage start with one of the four, hours before the craving shows up.
